flashcards.question: What is the primary architectural trade-off between Semantic Caching and Real-Time Vector Similarity Search?
flashcards.answer: Semantic caching achieves sub-5ms query times and saves API cost by matching cosine similarity against cached responses, but risks serving stale answers if underlying source documents update frequently.

full_articles.ai:
Title: Predictive Vector Cache Warming in Enterprise Agentic RAG
Source: Pinecone & OpenAI Research (2026)

Section 1: The Vector Search Latency Bottleneck.
In large-scale agentic RAG pipelines, computing dense vector embeddings and traversing billion-node HNSW graphs on every conversational turn creates 150-300ms latency overheads.

Section 2: The Two-Tier Cache Architecture.
By deploying Redis Semantic Cache in front of the vector database, queries with cosine similarity > 0.96 return pre-computed context chunks in under 4ms, reducing downstream embedding API costs by 42%.

Title: Context Window Compaction & Prompt Budgeting
Source: Anthropic & OpenAI (2026)

Section 1: Managing Context Bloat in Long-Running Workflows.
Passing raw chat histories across 20+ turns degrades LLM reasoning precision. Applying selective summarization and key-entity extraction preserves context fidelity within an 8k token envelope.
